system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: ∞-operad
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Cover infinity-operads as dendroidal inner Kan complexes, their relation to the underlying simplicial infinity-category, strict operadic nerves and the spine criterion, and the sufficient Kan condition on every operation space for a homotopy-coherent nerve. Distinguish inner, leaf, root and full horn conditions and uniqueness of fillers; exclude the construction and properties of the homotopy operad beyond the root-homotopy introduction on these pages, and exclude later model structures.

ATOMS:
- MATH-TOP-C01-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: A dendroidal set $X$ is an ∞-operad (a dendroidal inner Kan complex) if every map from an inner horn $\Lambda^e[T]\to X$ admits an extension to a map $\Omega[T]\to X$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s02] Deﬁnition 6.1 A dendroidal set X is a dendroidal Kan complex if any map from a horn Λx[T] →X admits an extension to a map Ω[T] →X.
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s06] A dendroidal set X is an ∞-operad or a dendroidal inner Kan complex if it satisﬁes this condition for every inner horn inclusion.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: An ∞-operad should be thought of roughly as a 'weak' operad in which composition is defined only up to homotopy.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s10] As with ∞-categories, one should think of ∞-operads roughly as ‘weak’ operads where composition is only deﬁned up to homotopy.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: A dendroidal set is a strict inner Kan complex (strict ∞-operad) when the extensions for inner horns exist and are unique.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s09] We will say X is a strict Kan complex if the necessary extensions are unique and similarly for strict inner, left, or right Kan complexes.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a dendroidal set $X$, being a strict inner Kan complex is equivalent to the map $X_T=\mathbf{dSets}(\Omega[T],X)\to\mathbf{dSets}(\mathrm{Sp}[T],X)$ being an isomorphism for every tree $T$, where the spine $\mathrm{Sp}[T]=\bigcup_{v\in V(T)}\Omega[C_v]$ is the union of the corollas of $T$.

    [MATH-TOP-p0231-s10] Proposition 6.4 For a dendroidal set X, the following are equivalent:
    [MATH-TOP-p0231-s11] (i) X is a strict inner Kan complex. (ii) For each tree T, the map
    [MATH-TOP-p0231-s12] XT = dSets(Ω[T], X) →dSets(Sp[T], X)
    [MATH-TOP-p0231-s13] is an isomorphism. (iii) X is isomorphic to NP for some operad P in Sets. (iv) The unit X →Nτ(X) is an isomorphism.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: A dendroidal set $X$ is a strict inner Kan complex if and only if $X$ is isomorphic to the nerve $N\mathbf{P}$ of some operad $\mathbf{P}$ in Sets, if and only if the unit $X\to N\tau(X)$ is an isomorphism.

    [MATH-TOP-p0231-s13] is an isomorphism. (iii) X is isomorphic to NP for some operad P in Sets. (iv) The unit X →Nτ(X) is an isomorphism.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: If $\mathbf{P}$ is a simplicial operad such that $\mathbf{P}(x_1,\dots,x_n;y)$ is a Kan complex for every tuple of colours, then its homotopy-coherent nerve $w^*\mathbf{P}$ is an ∞-operad.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0232-s19] Proposition 6.5 Let P be a simplicial operad such that for every tuple of colours (x1, . . ., xn, y) of P the simplicial set P(x1, . . ., xn; y) is a Kan complex.
    [MATH-TOP-p0232-s20] Then its homotopy-coherent nerve w∗P is an ∞-operad.
- MATH-TOP-C01-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: If $M$ is a simplicial set that is an inner Kan complex, then $i_!M$ is a dendroidal inner Kan complex, but this conclusion does not extend to dendroidal left or right Kan complexes.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s22] Also, if M is a simplicial set which is an inner Kan complex, then i!M is a dendroidal inner Kan complex.
    [MATH-TOP-p0229-s23] This last conclusion does not extend to dendroidal (left or right) Kan complexes.

    [MATH-TOP-p0230-s14] However, a map as indicated by the dashed arrow cannot exist because Cn is not a linear tree. □
- MATH-TOP-C01-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The nerve of a symmetric monoidal groupoid's operad $\mathbf{C}^\otimes$ is a dendroidal left Kan complex, not necessarily strict, so it satisfies the filling condition for leaf horns as well as inner horns, while the underlying simplicial set is strict as an inner Kan complex.
  EVIDENCE:

    [MATH-TOP-p0230-s24] Of course the underlying simplicial set i∗NC⊗, being simply the nerve of the groupoid C, is a Kan complex which is strict as an inner Kan complex (i.e., all ﬁllers for inner horns are unique).
